captions.detailed: This 3D model represents a BMX jump fork and steering assembly. It features a wide metallic triple-clamp crown securing two parallel round-section fork legs with an axle rod at the bottom, and a vertical steerer tube passing through a dark-colored frame head tube. At the top, a metallic quill stem clamps a pair of upswept riser handlebars finished with black textured grips. The entire steering assembly (fork, stem, and handlebars) is designed to rotate relative to the stationary head-tube frame mount on a continuous revolute axis.
captions.instruction: Generate a BMX jump fork assembly with a wide triple-clamp crown, parallel lower fork legs, a head tube frame mount, and upswept riser handlebars with black grips. The steering column should be connected to the frame mount via a continuous revolute joint to simulate steering rotation.
captions.factory: The model is constructed using an articulated object structure. It defines two main parts: a stationary 'head_tube' representing the frame mount, and a rotating 'steering_assembly'. The steering assembly is built by combining cylinders for the fork legs, steerer tube, and stem, box primitives for the triple clamps and handlebar clamp, and swept/extruded profiles for the riser handlebars and grips. A revolute joint named 'steering' is defined along the Z-axis, connecting the head tube to the steering assembly.
